svg.title: Densities of the sample mean at three sample sizes
svg.desc: Three exact densities of the sample mean from an Exponential population, at n equal to 1, 5 and 30, on a shared axis: the curves narrow around 1 and become steadily more symmetric, with a dashed normal curve almost covering the n equals 30 curve.
svg.text: What the central limit theorem is actually about
Exact densities of the sample mean from an Exponential(1) population.
normal with the same mean and variance
The population never changes: it is Exponential(1) in all three curves. What changes is the
distribution of the average. It concentrates on the mean, which is the weak law, and because
this population has finite variance the width shrinks like one over the square root of n. Only
after standardizing does it settle onto a fixed bell shape. At n = 30 the residual right
skewness is about 0.37, small but not zero.
